issues.summary: Improve retries on failed card payments
issues.description: About 4% of card payments fail on the first attempt, mostly PSP timeouts. Today the charge client retries twice with a fixed 500 ms delay, and it also retries hard declines, which the PSP flags as abusive traffic. We need one retry policy that the checkout, ops alerts and the charge client all follow.
comments: Numbers from last week: 61% of first-attempt failures are network timeouts, 22% are HTTP 503 from the PSP, 17% are card declines.
From the 3 Nov payments sync: We agreed payment retries are capped at 3 with exponential backoff. Hard declines such as insufficient funds or a stolen card are never retried.
Agreed with Ops: the whole retry sequence must finish within 30 seconds so the checkout page never times out.
Could we add jitter to the backoff? Let's try it in staging first; not decided yet.
Someone suggested 5 retries to be safe, but the PSP account manager said that would trip their rate limiter, so nobody agreed to it.

issues.summary: Fix retry logic in the charge client
issues.description: src/charge.js still uses the old behaviour (2 retries, fixed delay, retries every error). Bring it in line with the team's retry policy.

issues.summary: Checkout: show a 'still trying' message while a payment is retried
issues.description: Customers refresh the page when the spinner runs for more than a few seconds. Show a calm message between retry attempts. Copy depends on how many attempts we make.

issues.summary: Alert when the payment retry rate goes above 2%
issues.description: Ops wants a dashboard tile and a pager alert. The threshold math assumes the maximum number of attempts per payment.

issues.summary: Move refunds to the async queue?
issues.description: Open question from the 3 Nov sync. Nothing decided yet.

pages.title: Payments sync - 3 Nov 2026
pages.storage:
Attendees: Amara (payments lead), Jonas (backend), Priya (ops), Wei (checkout)

Discussion

Retry storms during the PSP outage on 28 Oct doubled our decline rate. Jonas walked through the timeout numbers from PAY ticket comments.

Decisions

  • Every charge request carries an idempotency key generated by the client, and the gateway rejects duplicates for 24 hours.

  • Amounts are stored as integer minor units (cents); floating point numbers are not allowed anywhere in the payments service.

  • Retries apply only to network timeouts and HTTP 5xx responses from the PSP, never to card declines.

  • PSP webhooks are the source of truth for the final payment status; the redirect result page is only a hint.

  • Card numbers are never written to logs, not even masked.

Open questions

  • Should refunds move to the async queue? Priya will check volume numbers before we decide.

  • Do we need a second PSP for failover? Not decided; revisit after Q1 costs are in.

Action items

  • Jonas: update the charge client to the new retry policy.

  • Wei: draft copy for the 'still trying' message.

pages.title: Payments service - onboarding notes (2025)
pages.storage:
Welcome to the payments team! A few things to know about the charge client.

  • Payment calls are retried twice on failure with a fixed 500 ms delay.

  • We use the sandbox PSP account for local development.

  • Ask in #payments before changing anything in the webhook handler.

Last reviewed: March 2025.

pages.title: PSP migration sync - 2 Dec 2026
pages.storage:
Attendees: Amara, Jonas, Priya

Context

The new PSP contract starts on 1 Jan. Their soft-decline guidance recommends up to five attempts, and their rate limits are per merchant per second instead of per minute.

Decisions

  • Because of the new PSP limits, we agreed to raise payment retries to 5 attempts with exponential backoff.

  • The total retry time stays under 30 seconds.

Open questions

  • Do we keep the old PSP as a fallback for one month? Amara to check the contract.
